meta.name: Anant Kumar
meta.title: Anant Kumar, AI engineer
meta.description: AI engineer. 55+ client pilots at IBM, 16 of 24 converted to paid work in the first year. Now studying for an MS in Computer Science at NYU Courant. Agents, retrieval and fine-tuned models that turn vague asks into exact outputs.
meta.ogImageAlt: A struck-through vague sentence above the exact one: AI engineer. 55+ client pilots. 16 of 24 converted in year one.

hero.vague: I do, sort of, AI things for big companies?
hero.intro: I'm Anant Kumar. People bring me a loose sentence about what they want, and I hand back something exact: Java that compiles, a test step precise enough to automate, an answer in under three seconds. I did that for three years at IBM. I'm now in New York, studying for an MS in Computer Science at NYU Courant.

pairs.heading: Six asks, six outputs
pairs.intro: Each project below began as a loose request. The asks on the left are my paraphrase of how such projects start, not client quotes. The outputs on the right are what I built, with the numbers I can stand behind.
pairs.hint: Each output starts out of focus and sharpens as you reach it. Drag the yellow line to pull it in or out of focus yourself.

items.ask: We have a lot of COBOL. Can AI make it Java?
items.title: ~250 COBOL files migrated to Java, about 75% compiling without manual fixes.
items.body: I fine-tuned Llama 3.1 70B with QLoRA to migrate COBOL to Java for major Japanese automotive and electronics firms. About 75% of the files compiled without manual fixes before human review, and client feedback guided the tuning.

items.ask: The test steps are all written down. They just need to be clearer.
items.title: Hundreds of ambiguous test steps rewritten as precise ones, ready to become Playwright tests.
items.body: I built LangGraph agents that turned hundreds of ambiguous test steps for a client's web app into precise ones. Three RAG pipelines gave them context from PDF documents, transcribed videos and source files. I then architected the next stage, which turns the refined steps into Playwright tests, and guided the leads who built it.

items.ask: It's in the financial statements somewhere. Nobody has time to look.
items.title: Question answering over 10K+ pages of financial statements: ~90% accuracy, under 3 s per answer.
items.body: A RAG system using hybrid search, with Milvus vector search and Elasticsearch BM25 side by side, followed by a reranker. Accuracy was measured on 100+ test questions.

items.ask: Could the planners just tell it what changed and run it again?
items.title: A scheduling model that planners re-solve by changing constraints in plain language.
items.body: I built a multi-agent layer with LangGraph and Granite over a major U.S. airline's CPLEX scheduling model. Planners change constraints in plain language and re-solve. I packaged it as a reusable demo for IBM sellers.

items.ask: We need new candidate molecules. Can a model propose some?
items.title: An app that generates candidate molecules as SMILES strings.
items.body: I created an app on IBM's SMI-TED foundation model that generates candidate molecules (SMILES) for a major Japanese materials company. I wrote its tests and its Tekton CI/CD pipelines, and it became a reusable IBM asset.

items.ask: I want to type what I'm looking for and get the right photo.
items.title: Natural-language image search for a public-sector client.
items.body: I fine-tuned Detectron to tag images and used GPT-3 to turn each query into JSON keywords, which were matched against those tags with full matches ranked first.
facts: GPT-3 for query to JSON keywords

stillVague.heading: Still vague
stillVague.intro: One question I haven't finished answering. It's my current research project.
stillVague.ask: Which functions should a coding agent actually read?
stillVague.title: Learned AST Pruning for Coding Agents
body: I'm building a 125M-parameter ranker (UniXcoder, contrastive InfoNCE loss) that picks which Python functions a coding agent sees under a token budget. Each AST node is kept whole, kept as a signature, or dropped.

It trains on gold-patch labels from SWE-bench and SWE-Gym, about 21K issues. I'm benchmarking gold-function recall on SWE-bench Lite against BM25, LongCodeZip and SWE-Pruner, and serving the ranker to agents as an MCP server.
stillVague.resultsNote: Not in yet. This part stays out of focus until they are.

record.heading: Record
items: 55+ client pilots delivered in 2.5 years at IBM Client Engineering.
16 of 24 first-year pilots converted to paid IBM engagements.
2024 Growth Award for the most pilot conversions.

items.summary: LangGraph agents and three RAG pipelines that made a client's test steps precise. Architected the Playwright stage that followed and guided the leads who built it.

55+ client pilots, running technical discovery with Japanese clients. Fine-tuning for COBOL-to-Java migration, multi-agent systems over a CPLEX scheduling model, RAG over financial statements, and a molecule generator on SMI-TED.
Trained an image-captioning model on Flickr8k with a ViT encoder and a GPT-2 decoder.

Built natural-language image search for a public-sector client. Automated first-round interview screening for sales hiring: Whisper transcribed the answers, GPT-3 summarized them against the interview questions, and HR made the final call.
Coursework: Fundamental Algorithms; Intro to Deep Learning and LLM-based Generative AI Systems.

items.name: Learned AST Pruning for Coding Agents
items.summary: In progress. A 125M-parameter ranker that decides which Python functions a coding agent sees under a token budget, trained on about 21K issues from SWE-bench and SWE-Gym.

items.name: SummarizeTube
items.summary: A fully local YouTube summarizer running Mistral-Small and Whisper. It transcribes only when captions are missing, answers questions across a whole playlist with RAG, and shares VRAM between the models. About 2 minutes per hour of video.
